gloss: fall; fall down, fall slain, fall to (one's lot); hiphil cause to fall, cast (lots)
summary: The verb is to fall: to go down from standing or from a height to the ground, as a man from his seat (1Sa 4:18), a wall (Jos 6:20) or a tree (Ecc 11:3). From that, scripture uses it of falling slain in battle (“how the mighty have fallen”, 2Sa 1:19), of a city or nation coming to ruin (“fallen, fallen is Babylon”, Isa 21:9), of falling on one's face before God or a man, of sleep, dread or Yahweh's hand falling upon someone, of a portion or a lot falling to a man, and of a word that “falls” to the ground unfulfilled (Jos 21:45); its opposite is קוּם “rise” (Amo 5:2; Mic 7:8). The hiphil is to make fall: to fell, throw down, kill, and above all to cast the lot (Psa 22:19; Jon 1:7) and so allot the land as an inheritance. The nouns name what has fallen: מַפֶּלֶת a fall or downfall (and a fallen carcass), מַפָּלָה a ruin, נֵפֶל an untimely birth; the Aramaic of Daniel and Ezra, the Peshitta, Ugaritic, Phoenician-Punic and Jewish Aramaic have the same verb.

words.gloss: fall; fall slain; fall prostrate; fall upon; fall to (one's lot); hiphil cause to fall, cast (lots), allot
words.summary: About 430 times, mostly in the qal (367) and the hiphil (61), with five hithpael and one pilpel. The qal's core is the movement down to the ground; the preposition and context say whether a man falls dead, falls on his face, falls upon an enemy, falls away to another king, or whether a lot, a portion or a word “falls”.

stems.gloss: fall, fall down; fall slain; come to ruin; fall prostrate; fall on the neck; fall upon (attack); desert to; (of sleep, dread, the hand of Yahweh) fall upon; fall to (one's lot); (of a word) fail; lie fallen; (of the face) fall

senses.definition: To go down, without intending it or by force, from standing or from a height to the ground or into a place: a man from his seat, a wall, a tree, an axe-head into the water, an animal into a pit.

evidence.note: Eli “וַיִּפֹּל from upon the seat backward … and his neck was broken, and he died”.
At the shout “וַתִּפֹּל הַחוֹמָה תַּחְתֶּיהָ”: the wall fell down flat (under itself).
“If a tree falls (יִפּוֹל) in the south or in the north, the place where the tree falls, there it will be.”
As one was felling (מַפִּיל, hiphil) a beam, “the iron fell into the water”: qal and hiphil in one verse.
Ahaziah fell through the lattice of his upper room and was injured.
An uncovered pit, “and an ox or a donkey falls there”.
A parapet on the roof, lest blood come on the house “if the one falling falls from it”.
“He who digs a pit will fall (יִפֹּל) into it.”
“If they fall, the one will lift up (יָקִים) his companion; but woe to the one who falls and there is no second to lift him up”: falling and being raised.
“As Yahweh lives, not one hair of his head shall fall to the ground.”
Israel shaken among the nations as in a sieve, “yet not a pebble shall fall to the earth”.
Rebekah saw Isaac “וַתִּפֹּל from upon the camel”: she came down quickly.
“The fire of God fell from the heavens and burned up the sheep.”
The curse of the woman suspected of adultery: Yahweh making “your thigh fall (נֹפֶלֶת) and your belly swell”.

senses.gloss: fall slain, fall in battle, die
senses.definition: To fall dead, by the sword or in judgment; often with חָלָל “pierced, slain” or בַּחֶרֶב “by the sword”. The commonest single use of the verb.

evidence.note: “The men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, וַיִּפְּלוּ חֲלָלִים on Mount Gilboa”: fell slain.
David's lament: “אֵיךְ נָפְלוּ גִבּוֹרִים”, how the mighty have fallen; again 2Sa 1:25, 27.
Of Abner, murdered: “a prince and a great man has fallen this day in Israel”.
“In this wilderness יִפְּלוּ פִגְרֵיכֶם”, your corpses shall fall: the judgment on the generation that murmured; also Num 14:32.
“Your enemies shall fall before you by the sword (לֶחָרֶב).”
“There fell of the people that day about three thousand men.”
“A thousand may fall at your side and ten thousand at your right hand; it shall not come near you.”
To Ebed-melech: “by the sword you shall not fall … because you have trusted in me”.
“You shall fall by the sword, because you have turned back from following Yahweh.”
Tyre's men “shall fall (יִפְּלוּ) in the heart of the seas on the day of your fall (מַפַּלְתֵּךְ)”: the verb and its noun together.

senses.gloss: fall, come to ruin (a city, a nation, a man)
senses.definition: Of a city, kingdom, house or man: to be overthrown and brought low. Its opposite is to rise or be raised up (קוּם), and it stands beside כָּשַׁל “stumble”.

evidence.note: “נָפְלָה נָפְלָה בָּבֶל, and all the images of her gods he has shattered to the ground.”
“נָפְלָה, she shall rise (קוּם) no more, the virgin of Israel; forsaken on her land, there is none to raise her up.”
“In that day I will raise up (אָקִים) the booth of David הַנֹּפֶלֶת, and wall up its breaches, and raise up its ruins.”
“Jerusalem has stumbled (כָשְׁלָה) and Judah has fallen (נָפָל), because their tongue and their deeds are against Yahweh.”
“Suddenly Babylon has fallen and been broken.”
The earth reels like a drunkard; its transgression is heavy on it, “and it shall fall and not rise again”.
“He who trusts in his riches shall fall, but the righteous shall flourish like a leaf.”
“Seven times the righteous falls and rises (וָקָם), but the wicked stumble into calamity.”
“Do not rejoice over me, my enemy: כִּי נָפַלְתִּי קָמְתִּי”, though I fall I shall rise.
“Yahweh upholds (סוֹמֵךְ) all who fall (הַנֹּפְלִים).”
“Though he fall, he shall not be cast headlong, for Yahweh upholds his hand.”
To the king of Babylon (Isa 14:4): “How you have fallen from the heavens, shining one, son of the dawn; cut down to the ground, you who laid low the nations!”
Haman's wise men: if Mordecai, “before whom you have begun to fall”, is of the seed of the Jews, “you will surely fall (נָפוֹל תִּפּוֹל) before him”.

senses.gloss: fall down (on the face), fall prostrate
senses.definition: To throw oneself to the ground on the face or at the feet of another: in awe before God, in worship, in entreaty or homage before a man. Often joined with הִשְׁתַּחֲוָה “bow down”.

evidence.note: “וַיִּפֹּל אַבְרָם עַל פָּנָיו, and God spoke with him.”
When the fire fell on Elijah's offering, the people “fell on their faces and said, Yahweh, he is God”.
Fire came out from before Yahweh and consumed the offering; the people shouted “and fell on their faces”.
“This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of Yahweh; and I saw, and I fell on my face (וָאֶפֹּל עַל פָּנַי), and I heard a voice speaking.”
Moses and Aaron “fell on their faces” to plead for the congregation.
Joshua “fell on his face to the earth and bowed down (וַיִּשְׁתָּחוּ)” before the prince of Yahweh's host.
Ruth before Boaz: “she fell on her face and bowed down (וַתִּשְׁתַּחוּ) to the ground”.
Abigail “fell before David on her face and bowed to the ground”; and fell at his feet to plead (1Sa 25:24).
Mephibosheth “fell on his face and bowed down” before David.
The Shunammite “fell at his feet and bowed to the ground” when Elisha gave her back her son alive.
Esther “fell at his feet and wept and implored him” to avert Haman's evil.
Judah and his brothers “fell before him to the ground” in Joseph's house; again Gen 50:18.
“I was afraid and fell on my face.”
Balaam, “who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling down (נֹפֵל), and his eyes uncovered”.

senses.definition: With עַל צַוָּאר: to throw the arms round another's neck in greeting or grief.

evidence.note: “Esau ran to meet him and embraced him, וַיִּפֹּל עַל צַוָּארָו, and kissed him, and they wept.”
Joseph “fell on the neck of Benjamin his brother and wept”.
Joseph met Jacob in Goshen “and fell on his neck and wept on his neck a long while”.
“Joseph fell on his father's face and wept over him and kissed him.”

senses.definition: With בְּ or עַל of an enemy: to come down on him suddenly in attack.

evidence.note: Joshua came against the kings at the waters of Merom “suddenly, וַיִּפְּלוּ בָּהֶם”.
“Sheba fell upon them (וַתִּפֹּל שְׁבָא) and took them, and struck the servants with the edge of the sword.”

senses.definition: With עַל or אֶל of a king or army: to go over to him from one's own side.

evidence.note: The captain seized Jeremiah: “אֶל הַכַּשְׂדִּים אַתָּה נֹפֵל”, you are deserting to the Chaldeans; Jeremiah: “I am not falling away to the Chaldeans” (Jer 37:14).
Nebuzaradan exiled “the deserters (הַנֹּפְלִים) who had fallen to the king of Babylon”.
“He who goes out and falls to the Chaldeans who besiege you shall live.”
“Some of Manasseh fell to David”; the Philistine lords feared “he will fall to his master Saul”.
Many from Israel “fell to him (Asa) when they saw that Yahweh his God was with him”.

senses.gloss: fall upon, come upon (sleep, dread, the hand or spirit of Yahweh)
senses.definition: Of something that comes on a man from outside him and overpowers him: deep sleep, terror and dread, the hand of Yahweh, the spirit of Yahweh.

evidence.note: “A deep sleep (תַּרְדֵּמָה) fell on Abram, and behold, a dread of great darkness was falling on him.”
“In visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men.”
“Terror and dread fall upon them; by the greatness of your arm they are still as a stone.”
Rahab: “your terror has fallen on us”.
“The dread of the Jews had fallen upon them.”
Egypt was glad when they left, “for the dread of them had fallen upon them”.
“The terrors of death have fallen upon me.”
“A great trembling fell upon them, and they fled to hide.”
“וַתִּפֹּל עָלַי שָׁם יַד אֲדֹנָי יַהְוֶה”: the hand of the Lord Yahweh fell upon me there.
“The spirit of Yahweh fell upon me, and he said to me, Speak.”

senses.definition: Of a lot cast, or a portion or inheritance of land: to fall to a man as his.

evidence.note: “They cast lots (וַיַּפִּלוּ גּוֹרָלוֹת, hiphil), and the lot fell (וַיִּפֹּל הַגּוֹרָל) on Jonah.”
“The lot eastward fell to Shelemiah.”
“This is the land that shall fall to you (תִּפֹּל לָכֶם) for an inheritance, the land of Canaan.”
“This land shall fall to you for an inheritance”; also Ezk 47:22, the sojourners “shall fall in an inheritance among the tribes”.
“Ten portions (חַבְלֵי) fell to Manasseh.”
“The lines (חֲבָלִים) have fallen to me in pleasant places; yes, my inheritance is fair to me.”

senses.gloss: fall (to the ground), fail, of a word
senses.definition: Of a promise or word: to fall to the ground unfulfilled. Scripture uses it almost only in the negative, that no word of Yahweh's has fallen.

evidence.note: “לֹא נָפַל דָּבָר of all the good word that Yahweh had spoken to the house of Israel; all came to pass (הַכֹּל בָּא).”
“Not one word has fallen of all the good words … all have come to pass for you; not one word of them has fallen.”
Solomon: “not one word has fallen of all his good word which he spoke by the hand of Moses his servant”.
“Nothing of the word of Yahweh shall fall to the earth … Yahweh has done what he spoke by Elijah.”

senses.definition: The participle and some finite forms describe the state of one who has fallen: lying dead on the ground, or lying spread out over a place, as an army encamped or a people settled.

evidence.note: “If one slain (חָלָל) is found … lying (נֹפֵל) in the field, and it is not known who struck him.”
“Behold, their lord was fallen (נֹפֵל) to the earth, dead.”
“Sisera lay dead (נֹפֵל מֵת), and the peg in his temple.”
The Philistines found Saul and his three sons “fallen on Mount Gilboa”.
“Between her feet he bowed (כָּרַע), he fell (נָפַל), he lay (שָׁכָב); … where he bowed, there he fell, destroyed.”
“Midian and Amalek and all the sons of the east lay (נֹפְלִים) in the valley like locusts for multitude.”
Ishmael's sons dwelt from Havilah to Shur; “over against all his brothers נָפָל”, he settled, as was said of him, “he shall dwell (יִשְׁכֹּן) over against all his brothers” (Gen 16:12).
The concubine “lying (נֹפֶלֶת) at the door of the house, her hands on the threshold”.
“Over against all his brothers he shall dwell (יִשְׁכֹּן)”: the word Gen 25:18 answers with נָפָל.

senses.definition: With פָּנִים as subject: the face falls in anger or dejection.

evidence.note: “Cain was very angry, וַיִּפְּלוּ פָּנָיו.”
Yahweh to Cain: “Why are you angry, and why has your face fallen (נָפְלוּ פָנֶיךָ)?”

senses.gloss: (of a supplication) fall before, be presented
senses.definition: With תְּחִנָּה and לִפְנֵי: a plea “falls” before the one entreated, as one who pleads falls before him.

evidence.note: “Perhaps their supplication will fall before Yahweh (תִּפֹּל תְּחִנָּתָם לִפְנֵי יַהְוֶה), and they will turn each from his evil way.”
Jeremiah to Zedekiah: “let my supplication fall before you”.
The remnant to Jeremiah: “let our supplication fall before you, and pray for us to Yahweh your God”.

senses.definition: With בְּיַד: to come into another's power.

evidence.note: David: “Let us fall into the hand of Yahweh, for his mercies are many; but into the hand of man let me not fall.”
Samson: “shall I now die of thirst and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised?”

senses.definition: In Isa 26:18 the verb stands for birth: after a labour that brought forth only wind, “the inhabitants of the world have not fallen”, that is, been born. The hiphil of the next verse and the noun נֵפֶל use the same picture.

evidence.note: “We were pregnant, we writhed, we gave birth as it were to wind; we have not wrought salvation for the earth, וּבַל יִפְּלוּ יֹשְׁבֵי תֵבֵל.”

senses.gloss: fall short of, be inferior to
senses.definition: With מִן: to fall below another, be less than he.

evidence.note: “I have a heart as well as you; לֹא נֹפֵל אָנֹכִי מִכֶּם”, I am not inferior to you; again Job 13:2.

senses.gloss: (of a matter) fall out, turn out
senses.definition: Of an affair: how it ends.

evidence.note: Naomi: “Sit still, my daughter, until you know how the matter will fall (אֵיךְ יִפֹּל דָּבָר).”

senses.definition: In the law of clean and unclean: what the carcass of an unclean creeping thing falls upon becomes unclean.

evidence.note: “Anything on which any of them falls (יִפֹּל) when they are dead shall be unclean.”
“He does not die but falls to bed (נָפַל לְמִשְׁכָּב)”: is laid up.

stems.gloss: cause to fall, fell, throw down; bring down, kill; cast (lots); allot; let (a word) fall; present (a supplication); bring forth

senses.gloss: cause to fall, fell, throw down; bring down, kill
senses.definition: To make a thing or a man fall: to fell trees, throw down a wall, knock out a tooth, let something drop, and of men, to bring them down by the sword.

evidence.note: Joab's men were battering “לְהַפִּיל הַחוֹמָה”, to make the wall fall.
“Every good tree you shall fell (תַּפִּילוּ)”; done in 2Ki 3:25.
Of Sennacherib: “I will make him fall (וְהִפַּלְתִּיו) by the sword in his own land”; fulfilled in 2Ch 32:21, “they made him fall there by the sword”.
“I will make them fall by the sword before their enemies.”
The strange woman: “many are the slain she has cast down”.
The wicked have drawn the sword “to bring down (לְהַפִּיל) the poor and needy”.
“You set them in slippery places; you cast them down to ruin.”
He swore “to make them fall in the wilderness, and to make their seed fall among the nations” (Psa 106:27).
“If he knocks out (יַפִּיל) the tooth of his servant, he shall let him go free for his tooth.”
“I will make the sword fall from his hand”; Ezk 39:3, the arrows from Gog's right hand.
The quails: “he let them fall in the midst of their camp”.
A stone cast “and he made it fall on him” without seeing him: manslaughter.
The judge “shall cause him to lie down (וְהִפִּילוֹ) and be beaten before him”.
The little horn “cast down to the earth some of the host and of the stars, and trampled them”.
“He shall cast down tens of thousands, but he shall not prevail.”

senses.definition: With גּוֹרָל, or alone: to cast the lot so that it falls, leaving the decision to God.

evidence.note: “Come, וְנַפִּילָה גוֹרָלוֹת, that we may know on whose account this evil is upon us.”
“They divide my garments among them, and for my clothing יַפִּילוּ גוֹרָל.” Fulfilled at the cross (Jhn 19:24).
“הִפִּיל פּוּר הוּא הַגּוֹרָל”: they cast pur, that is, the lot, before Haman; again Est 9:24.
Saul: “Cast (הַפִּילוּ) between me and Jonathan my son”; and Jonathan was taken.
The rest of the people “cast lots to bring one of ten to dwell in Jerusalem, the holy city”.
“We cast lots for the wood offering.”
The courses of priests and Levites fixed by lot before David.
The robbers' invitation: “cast in your lot among us; one purse shall be for us all”.
“You would cast lots over the fatherless.”
“He has cast the lot for them, and his hand has divided it to them by line; they shall possess it for ever.”

senses.definition: To make the land “fall” to the tribes as their inheritance, by lot.

evidence.note: “Only allot it (הַפִּלֶהָ) to Israel for an inheritance, as I have commanded you.”
“See, I have allotted to you these nations that remain, for an inheritance for your tribes.”
“He drove out the nations before them and allotted them (וַיַּפִּילֵם) an inheritance by line.”
“When you allot the land (וּבְהַפִּילְכֶם אֶת הָאָרֶץ) for an inheritance, you shall offer an offering to Yahweh, a holy portion of the land.”
“You shall allot it for an inheritance to yourselves and to the sojourners who sojourn among you.”

senses.gloss: cause (deep sleep, dread) to fall upon
senses.definition: To bring sleep or terror down on someone.

evidence.note: “וַיַּפֵּל יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים תַּרְדֵּמָה עַל הָאָדָם”, and he slept, and he took one of his ribs.
“Slothfulness casts into a deep sleep.”
“I have made anguish and terrors fall upon her suddenly.”

senses.definition: To let a word drop to the ground, so that it is not done; with a negative, to keep every word.

evidence.note: “Samuel grew, and Yahweh was with him, וְלֹא הִפִּיל מִכָּל דְּבָרָיו אָרְצָה.”
The king to Haman: “let nothing fall (אַל תַּפֵּל דָּבָר) of all that you have spoken”.
“They did not drop (לֹא הִפִּילוּ) any of their practices or their stubborn way.”

senses.definition: With תְּחִנָּה or תַּחֲנוּנִים and לִפְנֵי: to make one's plea fall before God or the king.

evidence.note: “Not for our righteousnesses do we present our supplications before you (מַפִּילִים תַּחֲנוּנֵינוּ לְפָנֶיךָ), but for your great mercies.”
Daniel “presenting my supplication before Yahweh my God for the holy mountain of my God”.
“I presented my supplication before the king.”

senses.gloss: let (the face) fall on, cast down (the light of the face)
senses.definition: Of the face: Yahweh's face falling on a man in anger; the light of a man's face cast down.

evidence.note: “Return, faithless Israel; לוֹא אַפִּיל פָּנַי בָּכֶם, for I am merciful.”
“The light of my face they did not cast down.”

senses.gloss: bring forth (from the womb, from the earth)
senses.definition: To make fall from the womb, give birth: in Isa 26:19 the earth gives birth to the dead.

evidence.note: “Your dead shall live; my corpse, they shall arise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust … וָאָרֶץ רְפָאִים תַּפִּיל”: and earth shall bring forth the dead.
The water of the curse “to make the belly swell and the thigh fall (וְלַנְפִּל)”.

stems.gloss: throw oneself down (before); throw oneself upon

senses.gloss: throw oneself down, lie prostrate (before Yahweh)
senses.definition: To cast oneself down and stay prostrate in prayer.

evidence.note: Moses: “וָאֶתְנַפַּל before Yahweh as at the first, forty days and forty nights; I neither ate bread nor drank water.”
“I lay prostrate before Yahweh the forty days and the forty nights that I lay prostrate, because Yahweh had said he would destroy you.”
Ezra prayed and confessed, “weeping and casting himself down (וּמִתְנַפֵּל) before the house of God”.

senses.definition: To fall on someone to overpower him.

evidence.note: Joseph's brothers feared he meant “to roll himself upon us, וּלְהִתְנַפֵּל עָלֵינוּ, and take us as slaves”.

senses.definition: Once, of the slain falling in Sidon.

evidence.note: “וְנִפְלַל חָלָל in her midst by the sword against her on every side.”

evidence.locator: Isa.21.9, נָפְלָה → πέπτωκεν; Amo.9.11, נֹּפֶלֶת → πεπτωκυῖαν; Num.14.29, יִפְּלוּ → πεσεῖται; Hos.10.8, נִפְלוּ → πέσατε; πίπτω renders נָפַל ×183

evidence.note: Isa 21:9's cry taken up: “ἔπεσεν ἔπεσεν Βαβυλὼν ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη”; again Rev 18:2.
James quotes Amo 9:11: “I will rebuild the tabernacle of David which is fallen (τὴν πεπτωκυῖαν)”.
Num 14:29: those who sinned, “whose carcasses fell (ἔπεσεν) in the wilderness”.
Hos 10:8 quoted: “they will begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us (πέσετε ἐφ᾽ ἡμᾶς), and to the hills, Cover us”.
The unbeliever “falling on his face (πεσὼν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον) will worship God”, as the Hebrew נָפַל עַל פָּנָיו.
“They shall fall by the edge of the sword”, as Hebrew נָפַל לְפִי חָרֶב.

evidence.locator: Gen.46.29, וַיִּפֹּל → ἐπέπεσεν; Gen.15.12, נָפְלָה → ἐπέπεσεν; Psa.16.6 → ἐπέπεσάν; ἐπιπίπτω renders נָפַל ×11

evidence.note: The father “ran and fell on his neck (ἐπέπεσεν ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ) and kissed him”, as Joseph and Esau (Gen 33:4; 45:14; 46:29).
The Ephesian elders “fell on Paul's neck and kissed him”.
“Fear fell upon him (φόβος ἐπέπεσεν ἐπ᾽ αὐτόν)”, as dread fell on Abram (Gen 15:12).

words.gloss: Nephilim (mighty men of old; the giants the spies reported)
words.summary: Twice, in Gen 6:4 and Num 13:33 (once spelled plene, נְפִילִים). Gen 6:4 says who they were: on the earth in those days and after, “the mighty men (הַגִּבֹּרִים) who were of old, men of name (אַנְשֵׁי הַשֵּׁם)”. In Num 13:33 the spies use the word for the sons of Anak, men so tall that “we were in our own eyes as grasshoppers”, in a report the text calls an evil report (Num 13:32). The word is formed from נפל, but scripture does not say why they bore the name: whether they were “fallen” ones, or ones who fell upon others, or something else, the text does not say, and no cognate has been found. So its tie to the root's sense rests on its form alone, which is why it has no cognate support of its own. Nothing in either passage calls them anything but men.

senses.gloss: Nephilim: mighty men, men of name, of the days before the flood and after

doctrine.statement: Isaiah sets two births side by side. Israel's own labour brought forth nothing: “we were pregnant, we writhed, we gave birth as it were to wind; we have not wrought salvation for the earth, and the inhabitants of the world have not fallen”, that is, been born (Isa 26:18). Then Yahweh's answer: “Your dead shall live; my corpse, they shall arise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust, for your dew is a dew of lights, and earth shall bring forth (תַּפִּיל, make fall from the womb) the dead (רְפָאִים)” (Isa 26:19). The dead are in the dust, not elsewhere; they live again when they arise from it. From the verses: what men could not bring to birth, God will: the earth itself gives birth to the dead at the resurrection.

Amos foretold the fall of Israel's house: “fallen, she shall rise no more, the virgin of Israel” (Amo 5:2). He ends with Yahweh's promise: “In that day I will raise up the booth of David that is fallen (הַנֹּפֶלֶת), and wall up its breaches, and raise up its ruins, and build it as in the days of old”, that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations called by Yahweh's name; Israel's captivity will be returned, they will build the waste cities, and “I will plant them upon their land, and they shall no more be plucked up out of their land which I have given them” (Amo 9:11–12, 14–15). At the council in Jerusalem James quotes it: God first visited the nations “to take out of them a people for his name”, and “after this I will return and will rebuild the tabernacle of David which is fallen” (Act 15:14–16). From the verses: David's house and kingdom, now fallen, will be raised up again in Israel's land as it was in the days of old, after a people has been taken from the nations for God's name; the restoration is on the earth, in the land given to Israel.

Isaiah 14 is “this proverb against the king of Babylon” (Isa 14:4). In it: “How you have fallen (נָפַלְתָּ) from the heavens, shining one, son of the dawn; you are cut down to the ground, you who laid low the nations” (Isa 14:12). He is brought down “to the grave (שְׁאוֹל), to the depths of the pit” (Isa 14:15); those who see him say, “Is this the man (הָאִישׁ) who made the earth tremble, who shook kingdoms?” (Isa 14:16); and he is not joined with the other kings in burial (Isa 14:20). From the verses: the one who has fallen from the heavens is a man, the king of Babylon; the heavens he fell from are the height of his rule over the nations, and his fall ends in death and the grave. The passage says nothing of an angel.

Job wishes he had been “as a hidden untimely birth (נֵפֶל), as infants who never saw light”, for “now I would have lain down and been quiet; I would have slept; then I would have had rest” (Job 3:13, 16). The Preacher says the untimely birth “comes in vanity and goes in darkness, and its name is covered with darkness; it has not seen the sun nor known anything”, and asks of the man who lived two thousand years, “do not all go to one place?” (Ecc 6:3–6). From the verses: the dead child and the dead man alike lie in darkness, at rest, knowing nothing; there is no life of the dead apart from the resurrection.

Falling on the face is the posture of worship before God (Gen 17:3; 1Ki 18:39), and also of homage and entreaty before a man (1Sa 25:23; 2Sa 9:6). Nebuchadnezzar commanded every people to “fall down and worship” his image of gold, on pain of the furnace (Dan 3:5–6); the three Jews answered, “we will not serve your gods nor worship the image of gold which you have set up” (Dan 3:18), and were cast in (Dan 3:23). When Cornelius “fell at his feet and worshipped him”, Peter raised him: “stand up; I myself also am a man” (Act 10:25–26); when John “fell at his feet to worship him”, the angel said, “see you do not; I am your fellow servant … worship God” (Rev 19:10; 22:8–9). From the verses: to fall down in worship belongs to God; an image may not receive it, and neither an apostle nor an angel would accept it.

Yahweh said of the generation that refused to enter the land, “in this wilderness your corpses shall fall” (Num 14:29, 32), and those who went up without him fell by the sword (Num 14:43). Hebrews asks, “with whom was he angry forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose carcasses fell in the wilderness?”, and concludes, “they could not enter in because of unbelief”, so “let us be diligent to enter that rest, lest anyone fall after the same example of unbelief” (Heb 3:17, 19; 4:11). Paul, telling how “in one day twenty-three thousand fell”, says these things were written for our admonition, “so let him who thinks he stands take heed lest he fall” (1Co 10:8, 11–12). From the verses: Israel's falling in the wilderness is a warning to those called now; men who have been delivered can still fall short of the promised rest through unbelief.

note: Root key נפל, which is BDB's own key for the verb and its nouns; no existing entry had this root. No letter of נפל is a merged one, so there are no sounds. BDB keys: n.ek.aa (verb, 434 tokens: qal 367, hiphil 61, hithpael 5, pilpel 1), xn.al.aa (Aramaic verb, 10), n.ek.af מַפֶּלֶת, n.ek.ab נֵפֶל, n.ek.ag נְפִלִים, n.ek.ac מַפָּל. מַפָּלָה (n.ek.ad, Isa 17:1) and מַפֵּלָה (n.ek.ae, Isa 23:13; 25:2) are one word in two spellings; the brief counts the same three tokens under both keys, so only n.ek.ad is named, as the README directs for keys listing the same occurrences. m.da.bb is a cross-reference with no tokens. Dan 7:20 וּנְפַלָה is Aramaic “fell” but is not among the ten tokens counted under xn.al.aa; it is cited all the same. Num 5:22 לַנְפִּל is cited under the hiphil (“to make the thigh fall”); check its stem analysis. Hos 14:1 in the brief is the Hebrew numbering (English 13:16). Peshitta words from SEDRA root 1191 NIL: lexeme 1996 NPL “fall” (157 tokens, all peal in SEDRA's analysis) and 1995 MPOLTA “fall, collapse” (Mat 7:27; Luk 2:34; 6:49); vocalised Syriac in the notes is copied from the database; the lemma מַפּוּלְתָּא is a standard form. Cognates: Ugaritic from Segert's glossary p. 194 (leaf 221) and §64 p. 89, OCR only; Krahmalkov pp. 332 and 300 from the pdftotext copy, page images not checked. Leads not followed: Arabic نفل, which a lead links to “fell to his share”; Lane's article (p. 3036) gives only “he gave him spoil”, “a free gift”, “a supererogatory gift or prayer”, with no sense “fall”, so it is left out rather than forced onto “fall to one's lot”. Ge'ez not consulted (Dillmann, Leslau). DULAT not consulted for the Ugaritic forms. Akkadian napālu and nappaltu are entered as possible only: Akkadian “fall” is maqātu, and napālu's core is “tear down, dig out”. נְפִלִים: per the task, only what Gen 6:4 and Num 13:32–33 show is written; nothing on angels or on the identity of the sons of God, which the passages do not settle. Doctrine topic king-of-babylon rests on Isa 14:4, 12, 15–16, 20 only.
